heard: Our galaxy is falling toward an invisible cosmic monster. We are hurtling through the dark at 1.3 million miles per hour. For decades, the thick gas and dust of the Milky Way completely blocked our view of this giant. In the 1980s, astronomers used infrared and X-ray telescopes to finally pierce this barrier. They discovered the Great Attractor, a gravitational basin holding around 100,000 galaxies. But astronomers quickly realize this region has far too little mass to cause such a violent pull. Instead, a much larger Titan called the Shapley supercluster is dragging the entire region. Cosmic expansion will eventually pull us away, but for now, we continue our plunge.
